A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Explanatory Instructions and DECVT research. Their text, figures, tables, mathematical content and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite retitling and rearrangement.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuned model outputs and quantitative evaluations, including image editing, generation, dense prediction and restoration results in Appendix B, Tables 5–7.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments in Tables 1, 2 and 7 and adds qualitative outputs and an instruction-feature analysis in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same token-based autoregressive VLM, image/text tokenization, pretrained initialization, next-token objective with z-loss, bidirectional training and inference procedure. BERT is introduced for supplementary analysis, not as a component of the proposed method.

E1.justification: DECVT sources, represented vision tasks and benchmark datasets remain unchanged. The additional segmentation and detection examples concern existing coverage: object detection already appears in v1 Section 2.1 and Figure 23. They add reported outcomes without establishing a distinct task requirement or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the corresponding image-editing, generation and dense-prediction/restoration tables, including Lumina-mGPT, PixWizard and the task-specific baselines. Appendix A also retains its instruction-generator comparisons. BERT serves as a feature extractor, not a new competing method.

E3.justification: The new Appendix D analysis extracts BERT instruction features, reduces them to two dimensions using PCA and randomly samples 100 features per task for visualization. Existing model training settings, benchmark splits, metrics and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds a feature-space analysis of relationships between task instructions in Appendix D, Figure 57. Figure 32 also extends the existing category-name versus descriptive-instruction comparison with two plant examples. These are limited additions to the supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports benchmark run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Randomly sampling 100 features per task for the new PCA visualization is an analysis setting, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 5–7 correspond to v3 Tables 7, 1 and 2 with unchanged numerical results; for example, the proposed model's Canny-to-Image F1 remains 20.69. New results are qualitative plant comparisons in Figure 32, detection outputs in Figure 53 and overlapping instruction-feature distributions in Figure 57.

T1.justification: The autoregressive probability formulation and distinctions between instruction-level and task-level zero-shot generalization are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised; the PCA discussion is empirical and interpretive.

C1.justification: The central contributions—explanatory instructions, DECVT and instruction/task-level generalization—remain. The revised introduction strengthens the versatility claim from handling a wide range of tasks to handling 'any combination of tasks,' a limited broadening of the stated contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly interprets overlapping instruction-feature distributions as the primary driver of zero-shot generalization, contrasting them with discrete task-specific instruction clusters. The existing limitations concerning failed task generalization, data noise, output instability and model capacity remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code and dataset access from a promised release in v1 to reported availability in v3, using the same repository link. This is a documented availability change; access was not independently verified. Existing implementation and dataset-construction details remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds BERT for the feature analysis and limited citations to Lian, Fu, Wei and Zhang in the related-work discussion and conclusion. The existing literature and positioning against vision generalists using terminological instructions are retained.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title, edits and consolidates the contribution statements, adds a short quantitative-results subsection and an Impact Statement, and updates affiliation and citation presentation. Most substantive prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is substantially reformatted: the abstract moves to the first page, Figure 1 moves to the second, and v1 appendix Tables 6–7 become main-text Tables 1–2. Figure 32 expands, Figures 53 and 57 are added, and running headers and caption formatting change throughout. The old video Figure 56 is retained as Table 8.

improvement.justification: Moving the quantitative comparisons into the main text makes the evidence easier to assess, while additional prompt-comparison and detection examples make model behavior more inspectable. Release information is also updated. These are limited gains: benchmark results and major limitations remain unchanged, and the new PCA visualization does not establish the stronger causal explanation or unrestricted task-combination claim.
